## Task

mend cannot reclaim a stale claim whose worker name is still alive (no claim-age check)

## Description

src/strand/mend.rs:66-96 releases an in_progress bead ONLY when its assignee has
no live PID:

    if live_worker_ids.contains(assignee.as_str()) {
        continue;
    }

There is no claim-age check anywhere in that loop. The only TTL in the module is
heartbeat_ttl, which gates heartbeat FILES, not bead claims. The bead updated_at is
never consulted. So the release condition is purely "is the worker process dead."

Because --count 1 workers relaunch under the same name indefinitely, an abandoned
claim held by a still-running name is skipped on every mend pass forever, no matter
how old. Observed in tradegraph 2026-08-17: claims aged 11-27h, skipped repeatedly
while the fleet ran, ready frontier pinned at 0.

This is the safety net failing. The claim leak upstream is needle-55ec0193; fixing
that reduces the inflow but does not make the net sound -- any future abandonment
path reproduces the starvation.

FIX (interim, no schema change): add a second, independent release condition on
claim age using updated_at, which is already in the store. Fires regardless of
holder liveness. Approximate -- any update refreshes updated_at -- but it would have
caught all 9 tradegraph cases.

FIX (durable): model a claim as a lease rather than an unbounded assignment --
(bead_id, holder, claimed_at, renewed_at, lease_ttl), renewed by the worker while it
is actively working THAT bead. Mend releases any expired lease regardless of holder
liveness. Notes on shape:
  - Key per CLAIM, not per worker. A per-worker "most recently claimed bead" record
    is insufficient and actively misleading: tradegraph-1s most recent claim was
    3.6h old and looked healthy while six older claims rotted behind it.
  - Prefer claimed_at/lease_expires_at columns on the issue row over a side table --
    a side table must stay consistent with issue.status and buys claim history that
    forensic.jsonl already provides.
  - The worker name is ALREADY passed at claim time (assignee, plus --actor), so no
    new CLI parameter is required.
  - Drive renewal from the existing heartbeat rather than adding a second timer.
  - Reclamation is safe because bead-rs already has OCC: if mend releases a bead a
    slow worker still holds, that workers later close hits --if-revision and exits 4
    instead of silently double-writing.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Mend releases a stale claim even when the assignee name has a live PID.
- Claim-age threshold is configurable.
- A test covers: live worker name + stale claim -> released.
- Renewal (if implemented) prevents reclaiming a genuinely active long-running bead.

//! Mend strand: maintenance and self-healing.
//!
//! Strand 2 in the waterfall. Runs after Pluck finds no work. Cleans up
//! stale claims, orphaned locks, broken dependency links, and database
//! corruption. If any cleanup is performed, returns `WorkCreated` so the
//! waterfall restarts from Pluck (released beads may now be claimable).
//!
//! Depends on: `bead_store`, `config`, `health`, `peer`, `registry`,
//!             `telemetry`, `types`, `trace`.

use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::{Duration, SystemTime};

use anyhow::{Context, Result};
use chrono::Utc;

use crate::bead_store::BeadStore;
use crate::config::{LimitsConfig, MendConfig};
use crate::health::HealthMonitor;
use crate::learning::LearningsFile;
use crate::peer::PeerMonitor;
use crate::registry::Registry;
use crate::telemetry::{EventKind, Telemetry};
use crate::trace::cleanup_traces;
use crate::types::{BeadId, BeadStatus, StrandError, StrandResult};

// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Store-scoped orphan cleanup (shared between Mend and Explore)
// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Scan all in-progress beads in a store and release any whose assignee does
/// not correspond to a live worker. This catches beads orphaned by workers
/// that died without leaving a heartbeat file (or whose heartbeat was already
/// cleaned up).
///
/// This is a store-scoped function that can be called against any BeadStore,
/// not just the home workspace. Used by both MendStrand (for home) and
/// ExploreStrand (for remote workspaces).
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `store` - The bead store to scan (can be home or remote)
/// * `registry` - Worker registry for live worker lookup
/// * `telemetry` - Telemetry emitter for orphan release events
/// * `qualified_id` - This worker's fully-qualified identity (excluded from orphan detection)
///
/// # Returns
/// * `Ok(u32)` - Number of orphans released
/// * `Err(anyhow::Error)` - Store read failure
pub async fn cleanup_orphaned_in_progress(
    store: &dyn BeadStore,
    registry: &Registry,
    telemetry: &Telemetry,
    qualified_id: &str,
) -> Result<u32> {
    let all_beads = store.list_all().await?;

    // Registry::list() does blocking file I/O and PID checks.
    // Use spawn_blocking to avoid blocking the async executor.
    let registry_for_blocking = registry.clone();
    let workers = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || registry_for_blocking.list())
        .await
        .context("spawn_blocking task for registry.list() failed")?
        .context("registry.list() failed")?;

    // Build a set of fully-qualified worker IDs for registered, alive workers.
    let live_worker_ids: std::collections::HashSet<String> = workers
        .iter()
        .filter(|w| HealthMonitor::check_pid_alive(w.pid))
        .map(|w| w.id.clone())
        .collect();

    let mut released = 0u32;

    for bead in &all_beads {
        if bead.status != BeadStatus::InProgress {
            continue;
        }

        let assignee = match &bead.assignee {
            Some(a) if !a.is_empty() => a,
            _ => continue,
        };

        // Skip if the assignee matches our own qualified identity (we're running).
        if assignee == qualified_id {
            continue;
        }

        // Skip if the assignee matches a registered, alive worker.
        // Workers register with fully-qualified IDs ({adapter}-{worker_id}),
        // so this comparison prevents collisions when workers from different
        // adapter pools share a NATO name.
        if live_worker_ids.contains(assignee.as_str()) {
            continue;
        }

        // Orphaned: assignee is not a live registered worker. Release it.
        tracing::info!(
            bead_id = %bead.id,
            assignee = %assignee,
            workspace = %bead.workspace.display(),
            "releasing orphaned in-progress bead (assignee has no live worker)"
        );

        match store.release(&bead.id).await {
            Ok(()) => {
                let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::BeadReleased {
                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),
                    reason: format!("orphaned: assignee {} has no live worker", assignee),
                });
                let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::StuckReleased {
                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),
                    peer_worker: assignee.clone(),
                });
                released += 1;
            }
            Err(e) => {
                tracing::warn!(
                    bead_id = %bead.id,
                    error = %e,
                    "failed to release orphaned in-progress bead"
                );
                let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::MendBeadReleaseFailed {
                    bead_id: bead.id.to_string(),
                    assignee: assignee.clone(),
                    error: e.to_string(),
                });
            }
        }
    }

    Ok(released)
}

/// Summary of work performed during one Mend evaluation cycle.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
struct MendSummary {
    beads_released: u32,
    locks_removed: u32,
    deps_cleaned: u32,
    db_repaired: bool,
    db_rebuilt: bool,
    agent_logs_cleaned: u32,
    zero_activity_logs_cleaned: u32,
    traces_pruned: u32,
    traces_cleaned: u32,
    learnings_pruned: u32,
    learnings_consolidated: u32,
    orphaned_heartbeats_removed: u32,
    workers_deregistered: u32,
    idle_workers_flagged: u32,
    rate_limits_cleaned: u32,
    rate_limit_providers_removed: u32,
    rate_limit_providers_reset: u32,
    assignees_cleared: u32,
}

impl MendSummary {
    /// Whether mend performed work that changes bead store state.
    ///
    /// Only operations that add or release claimable beads should return true.
    /// A strand MUST return `WorkCreated` only when it inserts a claimable bead
    /// into the store that the waterfall will re-scan. No-op cleanup (pruning
    /// traces, removing stale locks, repairing DB) should return `NoWork`.
    ///
    /// Operations that return `WorkCreated`:
    /// - `beads_released > 0`: Orphaned beads were released back to Open status.
    /// - `deps_cleaned > 0`: Stale dependency links were removed (beads become claimable).
    /// - `assignees_cleared > 0`: Stale assignees were cleared (beads become claimable).
    ///
    /// Operations that return `NoWork` (maintenance, not work creation):
    /// - `locks_removed > 0`: Lock file cleanup (doesn't add beads to queue).
    /// - `db_repaired`: Doctor repair fixed index corruption (doesn't add beads).
    /// - `db_rebuilt`: Full rebuild from JSONL (doesn't add beads).
    /// - `traces_pruned`, `agent_logs_cleaned`, `learnings_*`: File cleanup.
    ///
    /// A `WorkCreated` return must be paired with a telemetry event identifying
    /// the created bead(s) so operators can see what the restart is chasing.
    fn did_work(&self) -> bool {
        // Bead release, dependency removal, and assignee clearing add claimable items to the queue.
        // Lock removal, DB repair, and DB rebuild are maintenance operations
        // that don't create new work and must not trigger a waterfall restart.
        self.beads_released > 0 || self.deps_cleaned > 0 || self.assignees_cleared > 0
    }
}

/// The Mend strand — maintenance and self-healing.
pub struct MendStrand {
    config: MendConfig,
    heartbeat_dir: PathBuf,
    heartbeat_ttl: Duration,
    lock_dir: PathBuf,
    /// Fully-qualified worker identity ({adapter}-{worker_id}).
    /// Used for heartbeat file lookups and registry comparisons to prevent
    /// collisions when workers from different adapter pools share a NATO name.
    qualified_id: String,
    registry: Registry,
    telemetry: Telemetry,
    log_dir: PathBuf,
    retention_days: u32,
    traces_dir: PathBuf,
    trace_retention_failed_days: u32,
    trace_retention_success_days: u32,
    workspace: PathBuf,
    max_learnings: usize,
    /// Base state directory (contains `rate_limits/` subdirectory).
    state_dir: PathBuf,
    /// Provider/model limits configuration for rate limiter cleanup.
    limits_config: LimitsConfig,
}

use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::Duration;

use anyhow::Result;
use chrono::Utc;

// Import all necessary types directly
use needle::bead_store::{BeadStore, Filters};
use needle::health::HeartbeatData;
use needle::registry::Registry;
use needle::strand::{mend::MendStrand, Strand};
use needle::telemetry::Telemetry;
use needle::types::{Bead, BeadId, BeadStatus, StrandResult};

#[derive(Clone)]
struct SimpleStore {
    beads: std::sync::Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Vec<Bead>>>,
    clear_count: std::sync::Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32>,
}

impl SimpleStore {
    fn new(beads: Vec<Bead>) -> Self {
        Self {
            beads: std::sync::Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(beads)),
            clear_count: std::sync::Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32::new(0)),
        }
    }

    fn clear_count(&self) -> u32 {
        self.clear_count.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed)
    }
}

#[async_trait::async_trait]
impl BeadStore for SimpleStore {
    async fn ready(&self, _filters: &Filters) -> Result<Vec<Bead>> {
        Ok(vec![])
    }

    async fn list_all(&self) -> Result<Vec<Bead>> {
        Ok(self.beads.lock().unwrap().clone())
    }

    async fn show(&self, _id: &BeadId) -> Result<Bead> {
        anyhow::bail!("not implemented")
    }

    async fn claim(&self, _id: &BeadId, _actor: &str) -> Result<needle::types::ClaimResult> {
        anyhow::bail!("not implemented")
    }

    async fn claim_auto(&self, _actor: &str) -> Result<needle::types::ClaimResult> {
        anyhow::bail!("not implemented")
    }

    async fn release(&self, _id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }

    async fn block(&self, _id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }

    async fn flush(&self) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }

    async fn reopen(&self, _id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }

    async fn labels(&self, _id: &BeadId) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
        Ok(vec![])
    }

    async fn add_label(&self, _id: &BeadId, _label: &str) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }

    async fn remove_label(&self, _id: &BeadId, _label: &str) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }

    async fn create_bead(&self, _title: &str, _body: &str, _labels: &[&str]) -> Result<BeadId> {
        Ok(BeadId::from("test"))
    }

    async fn doctor_repair(&self) -> Result<needle::bead_store::RepairReport> {
        Ok(needle::bead_store::RepairReport::default())
    }

    async fn doctor_check(&self) -> Result<needle::bead_store::RepairReport> {
        Ok(needle::bead_store::RepairReport::default())
    }

    async fn full_rebuild(&self) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }

    async fn add_dependency(&self, _blocker_id: &BeadId, _blocked_id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }

    async fn remove_dependency(&self, _blocked_id: &BeadId, _blocker_id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }

    async fn clear_assignee(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {
        let mut beads = self.beads.lock().unwrap();
        if let Some(bead) = beads.iter_mut().find(|b| &b.id == id) {
            bead.assignee = None;
            self.clear_count
                .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
            println!("CLEARED assignee for bead {}", id);
            Ok(())
        } else {
            anyhow::bail!("bead not found")
        }
    }

    fn has_valid_store(&self) -> bool {
        true
    }
}

fn make_bead(id: &str, status: BeadStatus, assignee: Option<&str>) -> Bead {
    let dt = Utc::now();
    Bead {
        id: BeadId::from(id),
        title: format!("Bead {id}"),
        body: None,
        priority: 1,
        status,
        assignee: assignee.map(|s| s.to_string()),
        labels: vec![],
        workspace: PathBuf::from("/tmp/test"),
        dependencies: vec![],
        dependents: vec![],
        comments: vec![],
        created_at: dt,
        updated_at: dt,
    }
}

fn write_heartbeat(dir: &Path, data: &HeartbeatData) {
    let name = if data.qualified_id.is_empty() {
        &data.worker_id
    } else {
        &data.qualified_id
    };
    let path = dir.join(format!("{}.json", name));
    let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(data).unwrap();
    std::fs::write(path, json).unwrap();
}

fn make_fresh_heartbeat(
    worker_id: &str,
    qualified_id: &str,
    current_bead: Option<&str>,
) -> HeartbeatData {
    HeartbeatData {
        worker_id: worker_id.to_string(),
        qualified_id: qualified_id.to_string(),
        pid: std::process::id(), // Our own PID = alive
        state: needle::types::WorkerState::Executing,
        current_bead: current_bead.map(BeadId::from),
        workspace: PathBuf::from("/tmp/test"),
        last_heartbeat: Utc::now(), // Fresh
        started_at: Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::seconds(3600),
        beads_processed: 5,
        session: worker_id.to_string(),
        is_idle: false,
        current_task: current_bead.map(|s| s.to_string()),
        model: "claude-sonnet-4".to_string(),
        heartbeat_file: None,
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn test_bug_scenario() {
    // Setup
    let hb_dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let lock_dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let reg_dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();

    // Create heartbeat for worker "test-worker-1" working on bead "different-bead"
    let heartbeat = make_fresh_heartbeat(
        "test-worker-1",
        "claude-code-glm-5-test-worker-1",
        Some("different-bead"), // Working on DIFFERENT bead
    );
    write_heartbeat(hb_dir.path(), &heartbeat);
    println!(
        "Created heartbeat: worker={}, current_bead={:?}",
        heartbeat.qualified_id, heartbeat.current_bead
    );

    // Create an OPEN bead assigned to this worker but it's NOT the current_bead
    let bead = make_bead(
        "stale-assigned-bead",
        BeadStatus::Open,
        Some("claude-code-glm-5-test-worker-1"),
    );
    println!(
        "Created bead: id={}, status={}, assignee={:?}",
        bead.id, bead.status, bead.assignee
    );

    let store = SimpleStore::new(vec![bead]);
    let registry = Registry::new(reg_dir.path());

    let config = needle::config::MendConfig::default();
    let heartbeat_ttl = Duration::from_secs(300);
    let telemetry = Telemetry::new("test".to_string());

    let mend = MendStrand::new(
        config,
        hb_dir.path().to_path_buf(),
        heartbeat_ttl,
        lock_dir.path().to_path_buf(),
        "test-mend-worker".to_string(),
        registry,
        telemetry,
        PathBuf::from("/tmp/logs"),
        0,
        PathBuf::from("/tmp/traces"),
        30,
        7,
        PathBuf::from("/tmp/workspace"),
        80,
        tempfile::tempdir().unwrap().path().to_path_buf(),
        needle::config::LimitsConfig::default(),
    );

    // Run Mend
    let result = mend.evaluate(&store, &HashSet::new()).await;

    // Check: assignee should be CLEARED because heartbeat shows different bead
    println!("Mend result: {:?}", result);
    println!("Clear count: {}", store.clear_count());

    assert!(
        matches!(result, StrandResult::WorkCreated),
        "Expected WorkCreated after clearing stale assignee, got: {:?}",
        result
    );
    assert_eq!(
        store.clear_count(),
        1,
        "Expected exactly 1 assignee cleared, got: {}",
        store.clear_count()
    );
}

# NEEDLE Codex Guide

This file is the primary operating guide for Codex in this repository, both in
interactive sessions and when Codex runs headlessly as a NEEDLE worker. Inspect
the current repository state and the relevant source before relying on older
examples or planning documents.

## Project Overview

NEEDLE (Navigates Every Enqueued Deliverable, Logs Effort) is a Rust worker
binary. It selects and claims work through the repository's configured bead
backend, dispatches a coding agent, records telemetry, and routes every outcome
through an explicit state machine.

The primary backend is bead-rs (`bead`); bead-forge (`bf`) remains supported
for explicitly bound legacy workspaces. Check `.needle.yaml` and the `.beads/`
layout before running either CLI. Do not infer the backend from which binaries
happen to be installed, and never use one backend's repair or import command on
the other backend's database. `br` is retired and must not be introduced in
source, prompts, scripts, tests, or documentation.

## Working Safely

- Inspect `git status --short` before editing. Preserve unrelated user and
  worker changes in a dirty worktree.
- Multiple NEEDLE workers may share the same repository. Re-check files before
  modifying them and avoid broad rewrites that can overwrite concurrent work.
- **Do not create per-worker git worktrees to isolate concurrent workers** —
  a shared checkout is the intended model, not a bug to route around.
  Worktrees add disk and build-cache duplication without addressing the
  actual failure mode, which happens at the bead level: the same bead getting
  claimed and worked twice (confirmed 2026-08-09, commitgraph `cg-l0v0kc` —
  two byte-identical commits at the same second from two concurrent workers).
  The supported backends provide atomic claim operations, so avoid this by
  decomposing and dependency-ordering beads so the same unit of work is never
  independently claimable twice — see the target repo's own `AGENTS.md` for
  repo-specific guidance.
- Do not use destructive Git operations (`reset --hard`, forced checkout,
  forced push) to resolve unrelated changes.
- Forgejo (`git.ardenone.com`) is the authoritative remote. GitHub is a mirror.
  Push only to the configured `origin`, and never use `--force` or
  `--force-with-lease`.
- Keep commands suitable for unattended execution: avoid prompts, pagers, and
  commands that require an interactive terminal.
- Treat `docs/plan/plan.md` as architecture and design history. Verify current
  behavior in source and against the installed CLI before depending on old
  command examples.

## Rust Compatibility

The declared MSRV is Rust 1.75 (`Cargo.toml`). Do not add language features or
dependencies that require a newer compiler without intentionally updating the
MSRV and associated toolchain and CI configuration.

## Code Conventions

- Prefer `Result` and `?` for fallible operations. Do not hide operational
  failures with `unwrap()` or `expect()`. Reserve those calls for tests or a
  clearly documented invariant/unrecoverable initialization condition.
- Fallible public operations should return `Result`; infallible constructors,
  accessors, and pure transformations may return ordinary values.
- Match state and outcome enums exhaustively. Avoid catch-all `_` arms where a
  new variant should force an explicit decision.
- Emit telemetry for every state transition and terminal outcome.
- Preserve error context at process, filesystem, database, and parsing
  boundaries.
- Unit tests belong in `#[cfg(test)]` modules near their implementation.
- Integration and end-to-end tests belong under `tests/`.
- Use `#[tokio::test]` for asynchronous tests; do not introduce
  `tokio_test::block_on`.
- Prefer testing public behavior over implementation details.

## Critical Test Isolation

Any test that spawns the compiled `needle` binary as a real subprocess (for
example, `Command::new(CARGO_BIN_EXE_needle)`) must isolate both `HOME` and the
Explore strand's scan root.

Explore is enabled by default and otherwise scans under the real home
directory. An unisolated test can discover and mutate production bead stores.
This previously created hundreds of phantom beads across real repositories.

At minimum, give the subprocess a temporary home:

```rust
cmd.env("HOME", temp_dir.path());
```

Prefer also configuring `workspace_root` to a temporary fixture directory, or
disable Explore when the behavior under test does not require it. Never point a
test worker at `/home/coding` or another directory containing real projects.

## Verification

- Run `cargo fmt --check` for Rust changes.
- Run targeted tests for the modules or behavior changed.
- Run `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` when practical. Existing
  unrelated warnings must be reported distinctly rather than silently fixed as
  part of an unrelated task.
- On this host, the `cargo` wrapper may offload a clean repository to iad-ci and
  use a resource-limited local fallback for a dirty repository. Do not assume a
  command ran remotely; report what actually ran and its result.
- The authoritative full verification is the `needle-ci` workflow on iad-ci
  after a push to `main`. Do not claim full-suite success from targeted tests.
- If required CI fails, record the failure on the bead, fix it, and do not close
  the bead as successfully completed.

## Bead Workflow

Each bead supplies its own deliverables and acceptance criteria. Complete and
verify the requested repository work before closing it.

This repository is bead-rs-backed. Use:

```bash
bead close BEAD_ID --reason "Summary of what was done"
```

The close flag is `--reason`, not `--body`. When no code change is appropriate,
record the reason with a bead comment or another supported public `bead`
operation rather than creating an empty commit.

SQLite (`.beads/beads.db`) is the live store. `.beads/checkpoint/` is the
git-tracked durable checkpoint, and mutations do not flush it implicitly.

Flush explicitly before committing bead state:

```bash
bead sync flush-only
./scripts/checkpoint-publish.sh stage
```

The staging helper resolves and verifies the generation objects named by both
checkpoint pointers, stages those objects atomically with the pointers, and
removes superseded `objects/gen-*.jsonl` files from the working tree. Install
the tracked pre-commit check once per clone with
`./scripts/install-git-hooks.sh`. Do not use `git add -A` for checkpoint
publication.

`bead doctor` is read-only by default. If a database is missing, wrong-schema,
or corrupt, confirm the backend first and restore an empty native store from
the committed forensic checkpoint with the documented `bead init` plus `bead
sync import-only --restore-into-empty` procedure. Never delete or rebuild a
bead database without explicitly accounting for unflushed work.

## Commits

Use the bead identifier when the work is bead-driven:

```text
feat(needle-XYZ): short description
fix(needle-XYZ): short description
test(needle-XYZ): short description
```

Do not mix unrelated cleanup into the task commit. State which checks were run
and any remaining limitations in the final handoff or bead notes.

## Telemetry Contract

NEEDLE emits OpenTelemetry-compatible telemetry via OTLP. When modifying code that interacts with the telemetry system, maintain these semantic conventions:

### GenAI Attributes

The `agent.dispatch` span uses OpenTelemetry's `gen_ai.*` semantic conventions:

| Attribute | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `gen_ai.system` | AI provider (e.g., `anthropic`, `openai`) |
| `gen_ai.request.model` | Model identifier (e.g., `claude-sonnet-4-6`) |
| `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` | Input token count |
| `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens` | Output token count |

These attributes enable NEEDLE telemetry to integrate with GenAI-focused dashboards (Grafana GenAI app, Langfuse, Honeycomb AI, etc.).

### Resource Attributes

Every exported signal carries these resource attributes:

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| `service.name` | `"needle"` |
| `service.version` | Build version from `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` |
| `service.instance.id` | Worker ID (e.g., `needle-claude-anthropic-sonnet-alpha`) |
| `needle.session_id` | Per-boot random session ID |
| `host.name` | Hostname |
| `process.pid` | Worker PID |

For the complete semantic mapping of NEEDLE events to OpenTelemetry signals, see [`docs/plan/plan.md`](docs/plan/plan.md).

    43	/// * `registry` - Worker registry for live worker lookup
    44	/// * `telemetry` - Telemetry emitter for orphan release events
    45	/// * `qualified_id` - This worker's fully-qualified identity (excluded from orphan detection)
    46	///
    47	/// # Returns
    48	/// * `Ok(u32)` - Number of orphans released
    49	/// * `Err(anyhow::Error)` - Store read failure
    50	pub async fn cleanup_orphaned_in_progress(
    51	    store: &dyn BeadStore,
    52	    registry: &Registry,
    53	    telemetry: &Telemetry,
    54	    qualified_id: &str,
    55	) -> Result<u32> {
    56	    let all_beads = store.list_all().await?;
    57	
    58	    // Registry::list() does blocking file I/O and PID checks.
    59	    // Use spawn_blocking to avoid blocking the async executor.
    60	    let registry_for_blocking = registry.clone();
    61	    let workers = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || registry_for_blocking.list())
    62	        .await
    63	        .context("spawn_blocking task for registry.list() failed")?
    64	        .context("registry.list() failed")?;
    65	
    66	    // Build a set of fully-qualified worker IDs for registered, alive workers.
    67	    let live_worker_ids: std::collections::HashSet<String> = workers
    68	        .iter()
    69	        .filter(|w| HealthMonitor::check_pid_alive(w.pid))
    70	        .map(|w| w.id.clone())
    71	        .collect();
    72	
    73	    let mut released = 0u32;
    74	
    75	    for bead in &all_beads {
    76	        if bead.status != BeadStatus::InProgress {
    77	            continue;
    78	        }
    79	
    80	        let assignee = match &bead.assignee {
    81	            Some(a) if !a.is_empty() => a,
    82	            _ => continue,
    83	        };
    84	
    85	        // Skip if the assignee matches our own qualified identity (we're running).
    86	        if assignee == qualified_id {
    87	            continue;
    88	        }
    89	
    90	        // Skip if the assignee matches a registered, alive worker.
    91	        // Workers register with fully-qualified IDs ({adapter}-{worker_id}),
    92	        // so this comparison prevents collisions when workers from different
    93	        // adapter pools share a NATO name.
    94	        if live_worker_ids.contains(assignee.as_str()) {
    95	            continue;
    96	        }
    97	
    98	        // Orphaned: assignee is not a live registered worker. Release it.
    99	        tracing::info!(
   100	            bead_id = %bead.id,
   101	            assignee = %assignee,
   102	            workspace = %bead.workspace.display(),
   103	            "releasing orphaned in-progress bead (assignee has no live worker)"
   104	        );
   105	
   106	        match store.release(&bead.id).await {
   107	            Ok(()) => {
   108	                let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::BeadReleased {
   109	                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),
   110	                    reason: format!("orphaned: assignee {} has no live worker", assignee),
   111	                });
   112	                let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::StuckReleased {
   113	                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),
   114	                    peer_worker: assignee.clone(),
   115	                });
   116	                released += 1;
   117	            }
   118	            Err(e) => {
   119	                tracing::warn!(
   120	                    bead_id = %bead.id,
   121	                    error = %e,
   122	                    "failed to release orphaned in-progress bead"
   123	                );
   124	                let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::MendBeadReleaseFailed {
   125	                    bead_id: bead.id.to_string(),
   126	                    assignee: assignee.clone(),
   127	                    error: e.to_string(),
   128	                });
   129	            }
   130	        }
   131	    }
   132	
   133	    Ok(released)
   134	}
   135	
   136	/// Summary of work performed during one Mend evaluation cycle.
   137	#[derive(Debug, Default)]
   138	struct MendSummary {
   139	    beads_released: u32,
   140	    locks_removed: u32,
   141	    deps_cleaned: u32,
   142	    db_repaired: bool,
   143	    db_rebuilt: bool,
   144	    agent_logs_cleaned: u32,
   145	    zero_activity_logs_cleaned: u32,
   146	    traces_pruned: u32,
   147	    traces_cleaned: u32,
   148	    learnings_pruned: u32,
   149	    learnings_consolidated: u32,
   150	    orphaned_heartbeats_removed: u32,
   151	    workers_deregistered: u32,
   152	    idle_workers_flagged: u32,
   153	    rate_limits_cleaned: u32,
   154	    rate_limit_providers_removed: u32,
   155	    rate_limit_providers_reset: u32,
   156	    assignees_cleared: u32,
   157	}
   158	
   159	impl MendSummary {
   160	    /// Whether mend performed work that changes bead store state.
   161	    ///
   162	    /// Only operations that add or release claimable beads should return true.
   163	    /// A strand MUST return `WorkCreated` only when it inserts a claimable bead
   164	    /// into the store that the waterfall will re-scan. No-op cleanup (pruning
   165	    /// traces, removing stale locks, repairing DB) should return `NoWork`.
   166	    ///
   167	    /// Operations that return `WorkCreated`:
   168	    /// - `beads_released > 0`: Orphaned beads were released back to Open status.
   169	    /// - `deps_cleaned > 0`: Stale dependency links were removed (beads become claimable).
   170	    /// - `assignees_cleared > 0`: Stale assignees were cleared (beads become claimable).
   171	    ///
   172	    /// Operations that return `NoWork` (maintenance, not work creation):
   173	    /// - `locks_removed > 0`: Lock file cleanup (doesn't add beads to queue).
   174	    /// - `db_repaired`: Doctor repair fixed index corruption (doesn't add beads).
   175	    /// - `db_rebuilt`: Full rebuild from JSONL (doesn't add beads).
   176	    /// - `traces_pruned`, `agent_logs_cleaned`, `learnings_*`: File cleanup.
   177	    ///
   178	    /// A `WorkCreated` return must be paired with a telemetry event identifying
   179	    /// the created bead(s) so operators can see what the restart is chasing.
   180	    fn did_work(&self) -> bool {
   180	    fn did_work(&self) -> bool {
   181	        // Bead release, dependency removal, and assignee clearing add claimable items to the queue.
   182	        // Lock removal, DB repair, and DB rebuild are maintenance operations
   183	        // that don't create new work and must not trigger a waterfall restart.
   184	        self.beads_released > 0 || self.deps_cleaned > 0 || self.assignees_cleared > 0
   185	    }
   186	}
   187	
   188	/// The Mend strand — maintenance and self-healing.
   189	pub struct MendStrand {
   190	    config: MendConfig,
   191	    heartbeat_dir: PathBuf,
   192	    heartbeat_ttl: Duration,
   193	    lock_dir: PathBuf,
   194	    /// Fully-qualified worker identity ({adapter}-{worker_id}).
   195	    /// Used for heartbeat file lookups and registry comparisons to prevent
   196	    /// collisions when workers from different adapter pools share a NATO name.
   197	    qualified_id: String,
   198	    registry: Registry,
   199	    telemetry: Telemetry,
   200	    log_dir: PathBuf,
   201	    retention_days: u32,
   202	    traces_dir: PathBuf,
   203	    trace_retention_failed_days: u32,
   204	    trace_retention_success_days: u32,
   205	    workspace: PathBuf,
   206	    max_learnings: usize,
   207	    /// Base state directory (contains `rate_limits/` subdirectory).
   208	    state_dir: PathBuf,
   209	    /// Provider/model limits configuration for rate limiter cleanup.
   210	    limits_config: LimitsConfig,
   211	}
   212	
   213	impl MendStrand {
   214	    /// Create a new MendStrand.
   215	    ///
   216	    /// - `config`: mend strand configuration
   217	    /// - `heartbeat_dir`: path to `~/.needle/state/heartbeats/`
   218	    /// - `heartbeat_ttl`: how long before a heartbeat is considered stale
   219	    /// - `lock_dir`: directory where claim lock files live (default: `/tmp`)
   220	    /// - `qualified_id`: fully-qualified worker identity ({adapter}-{worker_id})
   221	    /// - `registry`: worker state registry
   222	    /// - `telemetry`: telemetry emitter
   223	    /// - `log_dir`: directory where agent log files live
   224	    /// - `retention_days`: number of days to retain agent log files (0 = disabled)
   225	    /// - `traces_dir`: directory where trace files live (`.beads/traces`)
   226	    /// - `trace_retention_failed_days`: retention days for failed bead traces
   227	    /// - `trace_retention_success_days`: retention days for successful bead traces
   228	    /// - `workspace`: workspace root path for learning consolidation
   229	    /// - `max_learnings`: maximum number of learning entries before consolidation
   230	    /// - `state_dir`: base state directory (contains `rate_limits/` subdirectory)
   231	    /// - `limits_config`: provider/model limits configuration for rate limiter cleanup
   232	    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
   233	    pub fn new(
   234	        config: MendConfig,
   235	        heartbeat_dir: PathBuf,
   236	        heartbeat_ttl: Duration,
   237	        lock_dir: PathBuf,
   238	        qualified_id: String,
   239	        registry: Registry,
   240	        telemetry: Telemetry,
   241	        log_dir: PathBuf,
   242	        retention_days: u32,
   243	        traces_dir: PathBuf,
   244	        trace_retention_failed_days: u32,
   245	        trace_retention_success_days: u32,
   246	        workspace: PathBuf,
   247	        max_learnings: usize,
   248	        state_dir: PathBuf,
   249	        limits_config: LimitsConfig,
   250	    ) -> Self {
   251	        MendStrand {
   252	            config,
   253	            heartbeat_dir,
   254	            heartbeat_ttl,
   255	            lock_dir,
   256	            qualified_id,
   257	            registry,
   258	            telemetry,
   259	            log_dir,
   260	            retention_days,
   261	            traces_dir,
   262	            trace_retention_failed_days,
   263	            trace_retention_success_days,
   264	            workspace,
   265	            max_learnings,
   266	            state_dir,
   267	            limits_config,
   268	        }
   269	    }
   270	
   271	    // ── Step 1: Stale claim cleanup via peer monitoring ──────────────────────
   272	
   273	    /// Check for crashed workers and release their orphaned beads.
   274	    async fn cleanup_stale_claims(
   275	        &self,
   276	        store: &dyn BeadStore,
   277	        summary: &mut MendSummary,
   278	    ) -> Result<()> {
   279	        let peer_monitor = PeerMonitor::new(
   280	            self.heartbeat_dir.clone(),
   281	            self.heartbeat_ttl,
   282	            self.qualified_id.clone(),
   283	            store,
   284	            &self.registry,
   285	            self.telemetry.clone(),
   286	        );
   287	
   288	        let peer_result = peer_monitor.check_peers().await?;
   289	        summary.beads_released += peer_result.beads_released;
   290	
   291	        Ok(())
   292	    }
   293	
   294	    // ── Step 1.5: Orphaned in-progress bead recovery ────────────────────────
   295	
   296	    /// Scan all in-progress beads and release any whose assignee does not
   297	    /// correspond to a live worker. This catches beads orphaned by workers
   298	    /// that died without leaving a heartbeat file (or whose heartbeat was
   299	    /// already cleaned up).
   300	    async fn cleanup_orphaned_in_progress(
   301	        &self,
   302	        store: &dyn BeadStore,
   303	        summary: &mut MendSummary,
   304	    ) -> Result<()> {
   305	        let released = super::mend::cleanup_orphaned_in_progress(
   306	            store,
   307	            &self.registry,
   308	            &self.telemetry,
   309	            &self.qualified_id,
   310	        )
   311	        .await?;
   312	        summary.beads_released += released;
   313	        Ok(())
   314	    }
   315	
   316	    // ── Step 1.6: Stale assignee cleanup on open beads ─────────────────────────
   317	
   318	    /// Scan all open beads and clear assignees whose workers have no live heartbeat.
   319	    ///
   320	    /// This heals beads that became permanently unclaimable after a reopen
   321	    /// (bead-forge's reopen does not clear assignee). An open bead with a stale
   322	    /// assignee is invisible to all workers because ready() filters out assigned
   323	    /// beads. Clearing the assignee makes it claimable again.
   324	    async fn cleanup_stale_assignees_on_open_beads(
   325	        &self,
   326	        store: &dyn BeadStore,
   327	        summary: &mut MendSummary,
   328	    ) -> Result<()> {
   329	        let all_beads = store.list_all().await?;
   330	        let workers = self.registry.list()?;
   331	
   332	        // Build a set of fully-qualified worker IDs for registered, alive workers.
   333	        let live_worker_ids: std::collections::HashSet<String> = workers
   334	            .iter()
   335	            .filter(|w| HealthMonitor::check_pid_alive(w.pid))
   336	            .map(|w| w.id.clone())
   337	            .collect();
   338	
   339	        for bead in &all_beads {
   340	            // Only check open beads with an assignee.
   341	            if bead.status != BeadStatus::Open {
   342	                continue;
   343	            }
   344	
   345	            let assignee = match &bead.assignee {
   346	                Some(a) if !a.is_empty() => a,
   347	                _ => continue,
   348	            };
   349	
   350	            // Skip if the assignee matches our own qualified identity (we're running).
   351	            if assignee == &self.qualified_id {
   352	                continue;
   353	            }
   354	
   355	            // Skip if the assignee matches a registered, alive worker.
   356	            // Workers register with fully-qualified IDs ({adapter}-{worker_id}),
   357	            // so this comparison prevents collisions when workers from different
   358	            // adapter pools share a NATO name.
   359	            if live_worker_ids.contains(assignee.as_str()) {
   360	                continue;
   361	            }
   362	
   363	            // Stale assignee: clear it so the bead becomes claimable again.
   364	            tracing::info!(
   365	                bead_id = %bead.id,
   366	                assignee = %assignee,
   367	                workspace = %bead.workspace.display(),
   368	                "clearing stale assignee from open bead (assignee has no live worker)"
   369	            );
   370	
   371	            match store.clear_assignee(&bead.id).await {
   372	                Ok(()) => {
   373	                    let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MendStaleAssigneeCleared {
   374	                        bead_id: bead.id.clone(),
   375	                        assignee: assignee.clone(),
   376	                    });
   377	                    summary.assignees_cleared += 1;
   378	                }
   379	                Err(e) => {
   380	                    tracing::warn!(
   381	                        bead_id = %bead.id,
   382	                        assignee = %assignee,
   383	                        error = %e,
   384	                        "failed to clear stale assignee from open bead"
   385	                    );
   386	                    let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MendAssigneeClearFailed {
   387	                        bead_id: bead.id.to_string(),
   388	                        assignee: assignee.clone(),
   389	                        error: e.to_string(),
   390	                    });
   391	                }
   392	            }
   393	        }
   394	
   395	        Ok(())
   396	    }
   397	
   398	    // ── Step 1.75: Orphaned heartbeat file removal ────────────────────────────
   399	
   400	    /// Remove heartbeat files that have no matching entry in the worker registry.
   401	    ///
   402	    /// This can happen due to:
   403	    /// - Manual deletion of registry entries
   404	    /// - Registry corruption
   405	    /// - Worker crash between registry write and heartbeat file creation
   406	    ///
   407	    /// Only removes heartbeat files older than heartbeat_ttl to avoid deleting
   408	    /// recently orphaned files that might still be in use.
   409	    fn cleanup_orphaned_heartbeats(&self, summary: &mut MendSummary) -> Result<()> {
   410	        // Read all heartbeat files.
   411	        let heartbeats = match HealthMonitor::read_all_heartbeats(&self.heartbeat_dir) {
   412	            Ok(h) => h,
   413	            Err(e) => {
   414	                tracing::debug!(
   415	                    error = %e,
   416	                    "mend: failed to read heartbeat directory for orphaned heartbeat cleanup"
   417	                );
   418	                return Ok(());
   419	            }
   420	        };
   421	
   422	        // Get all registered worker IDs.
   423	        let registered_ids = match self.registry.list() {
   424	            Ok(workers) => {
   425	                let mut ids = std::collections::HashSet::new();
   426	                for w in workers {
   427	                    ids.insert(w.id);
   428	                }
   429	                ids
   430	            }
   430	            }
   431	            Err(e) => {
   432	                tracing::warn!(
   433	                    error = %e,
   434	                    "mend: failed to read worker registry for orphaned heartbeat cleanup"
   435	                );
   436	                return Ok(());
   437	            }
   438	        };
   439	
   440	        for hb in heartbeats {
   441	            // Use qualified_id for comparison; fall back to worker_id for old heartbeats.
   442	            let worker_key = if hb.qualified_id.is_empty() {
   443	                &hb.worker_id
   444	            } else {
   445	                &hb.qualified_id
   446	            };
   447	
   448	            // Skip if this heartbeat has a matching registry entry.
   449	            if registered_ids.contains(worker_key) {
   450	                continue;
   451	            }
   452	
   453	            // Skip our own heartbeat (shouldn't happen, but be safe).
   454	            if worker_key == &self.qualified_id {
   455	                continue;
   456	            }
   457	
   458	            // Check if the heartbeat is stale (older than TTL).
   459	            // Only remove stale heartbeats to avoid deleting recently orphaned files.
   460	            if !HealthMonitor::is_stale(&hb, self.heartbeat_ttl) {
   461	                continue;
   462	            }
   463	
   464	            // Heartbeat is orphaned and stale — remove it.
   465	            let heartbeat_path = hb
   466	                .heartbeat_file
   467	                .clone()
   468	                .unwrap_or_else(|| self.heartbeat_dir.join(format!("{}.json", worker_key)));
   469	
   470	            let age_secs = match file_age(&heartbeat_path) {
   471	                Some(age) => age.as_secs(),
   472	                None => continue,
   473	            };
   474	
   475	            match std::fs::remove_file(&heartbeat_path) {
   476	                Ok(()) => {
   477	                    tracing::info!(
   478	                        worker_id = %worker_key,
   479	                        path = %heartbeat_path.display(),
   480	                        age_secs,
   481	                        "removed orphaned heartbeat file"
   482	                    );
   483	
   484	                    let _ = self
   485	                        .telemetry
   486	                        .emit(EventKind::MendOrphanedHeartbeatRemoved {
   487	                            worker_id: worker_key.clone(),
   488	                            age_secs,
   489	                        });
   490	
   491	                    summary.orphaned_heartbeats_removed += 1;
   492	                }
   493	                Err(e) => {
   494	                    tracing::warn!(
   495	                        path = %heartbeat_path.display(),
   496	                        error = %e,
   497	                        "failed to remove orphaned heartbeat file"
   498	                    );
   499	                }
   500	            }
   501	        }
   502	
   503	        Ok(())
   504	    }
   505	
   506	    // ── Step 2: Orphaned lock file removal ───────────────────────────────────
   507	
   508	    /// Remove claim lock files that are not actively held by any process.
   509	    ///
   510	    /// This function immediately cleans up lock files whose holding process
   511	    /// has died, without waiting for an age-based timeout. The flock(2) lock
   512	    /// is automatically released by the kernel when the holder process dies,
   513	    /// so try_acquire_flock() will succeed immediately and we can remove the
   514	    /// stale metadata file.
   515	    ///
   516	    /// Lock files older than lock_ttl_secs are also cleaned up as a fallback
   517	    /// to handle edge cases where the flock probe might fail.
   518	    fn cleanup_orphaned_locks(&self, summary: &mut MendSummary) -> Result<()> {
   519	        let lock_ttl = Duration::from_secs(self.config.lock_ttl_secs);
   520	
   521	        let entries = match std::fs::read_dir(&self.lock_dir) {
   522	            Ok(e) => e,
   523	            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(()),
   524	            Err(e) => {
   525	                tracing::warn!(
   526	                    dir = %self.lock_dir.display(),
   527	                    error = %e,
   528	                    "failed to read lock directory"
   529	                );
   530	                return Ok(());
   531	            }
   532	        };
   533	
   534	        for entry in entries {
   535	            let entry = match entry {
   536	                Ok(e) => e,
   537	                Err(_) => continue,
   538	            };
   539	
   540	            let path = entry.path();
   541	            let name = match path.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str()) {
   542	                Some(n) => n,
   543	                None => continue,
   544	            };
   545	
   546	            // Only consider needle claim lock files.
   547	            if !name.starts_with("needle-claim-") || !name.ends_with(".lock") {
   548	                continue;
   549	            }
   550	
   551	            // Check file age for logging/fallback cleanup.
   552	            let age = match file_age(&path) {
   553	                Some(age) => age,
   554	                None => continue,
   555	            };
   556	
   557	            // Try to acquire flock (non-blocking). If we can acquire it,
   558	            // no one is holding it — safe to delete immediately.
   559	            //
   560	            // The kernel releases flocks when the holder process dies, so this
   561	            // probe succeeds immediately for dead PIDs regardless of file age.
   562	            match try_acquire_flock(&path) {
   563	                Ok(Some(_file)) => {
   564	                    // Lock acquired — no one holds it. Remove the file.
   565	                    let age_secs = age.as_secs();
   566	                    if let Err(e) = std::fs::remove_file(&path) {
   567	                        tracing::warn!(
   568	                            path = %path.display(),
   569	                            error = %e,
   570	                            "failed to remove orphaned lock file"
   571	                        );
   572	                        let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MendLockRemoveFailed {
   573	                            lock_path: path.display().to_string(),
   574	                            error: e.to_string(),
   575	                        });
   576	                        continue;
   577	                    }
   578	
   579	                    tracing::info!(
   580	                        path = %path.display(),
   581	                        age_secs,
   582	                        "removed orphaned lock file"
   583	                    );
   584	
   585	                    let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MendOrphanedLockRemoved {
   586	                        lock_path: path.display().to_string(),
   587	                        age_secs,
   588	                    });
   589	
   590	                    summary.locks_removed += 1;
   591	                }
   592	                Ok(None) => {
   593	                    // Lock is actively held — skip.
   594	                    // Only log if the file is old; otherwise it's just a normal active lock.
   595	                    if age > lock_ttl {
   596	                        tracing::debug!(
   597	                            path = %path.display(),
   598	                            age_secs = age.as_secs(),
   599	                            "lock file is old but actively held, skipping"
   600	                        );
   601	                    }
   602	                }
   603	                Err(e) => {
   604	                    tracing::debug!(
   605	                        path = %path.display(),
   606	                        error = %e,
   607	                        "failed to probe lock file"
   608	                    );
   609	                }
   610	            }
   611	        }
   612	
   613	        Ok(())
   614	    }
   615	
   616	    // ── Step 3: Dependency link repair ───────────────────────────────────────
   617	
   618	    /// Find open beads that have closed blockers and clean up the stale
   619	    /// dependency links.
   620	    ///
   621	    /// br does not automatically resolve dependency links on bead closure,
   622	    /// so a bead can remain blocked even after its blocker is closed.
   623	    async fn cleanup_stale_dependencies(
   624	        &self,
   625	        store: &dyn BeadStore,
   626	        summary: &mut MendSummary,
   627	    ) -> Result<()> {
   628	        let all_beads = store.list_all().await?;
   629	
   630	        for bead in &all_beads {
   631	            // Only check open beads that have dependencies.
   632	            if bead.status != BeadStatus::Open || bead.dependencies.is_empty() {
   633	                continue;
   634	            }
   635	
   636	            for dep in &bead.dependencies {
   637	                // Only check "blocks" type dependencies where the blocker is closed.
   638	                if dep.dependency_type != "blocks" {
   639	                    continue;
   640	                }
   641	
   642	                if dep.status == "closed" {
   643	                    tracing::info!(
   644	                        bead_id = %bead.id,
   645	                        blocker_id = %dep.id,
   646	                        "removing stale dependency link (closed blocker on open bead)"
   647	                    );
   648	
   649	                    // Remove the stale dependency link.
   650	                    match store.remove_dependency(&bead.id, &dep.id).await {
   651	                        Ok(()) => {
   652	                            // Emit telemetry for the removed dependency.
   653	                            let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MendDependencyRemoved {
   654	                                bead_id: bead.id.clone(),
   655	                                blocker_id: dep.id.clone(),
   656	                            });
   657	                            summary.deps_cleaned += 1;
   658	                        }
   659	                        Err(e) => {
   660	                            tracing::warn!(
   661	                                bead_id = %bead.id,
   662	                                blocker_id = %dep.id,
   663	                                error = %e,
   664	                                "failed to remove stale dependency link"
   665	                            );
   666	                            let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MendDependencyCleanupFailed {
   667	                                bead_id: bead.id.to_string(),
   668	                                blocker_id: dep.id.to_string(),
   669	                                error: e.to_string(),
   670	                            });
   671	                        }
   672	                    }
   673	                }
   674	            }
   675	        }
   676	
   677	        Ok(())
   678	    }
   679	
   680	    // ── Step 3.5: Dead worker registry cleanup ───────────────────────────────
   681	
   682	    /// Scan the worker registry and remove entries for dead PIDs.
   683	    ///
   684	    /// This proactive cleanup ensures that dead worker entries don't accumulate
   685	    /// in the registry. The registry's list() method already filters dead PIDs,
   686	    /// but that only happens when rate limit checks run. This step ensures
   687	    /// cleanup happens every mend cycle.
   688	    fn cleanup_dead_workers(&self, summary: &mut MendSummary) -> Result<()> {
   689	        // Read the raw registry file to find entries that need cleanup.
   690	        let raw_content = match std::fs::read_to_string(self.registry.path()) {
   691	            Ok(c) => c,
   692	            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(()),
   693	            Err(e) => {
   694	                tracing::warn!(error = %e, "failed to read registry file");
   695	                return Ok(());
   696	            }
   697	        };
   698	
   699	        let raw_reg: crate::registry::RegistryFile = match serde_json::from_str(&raw_content) {
   700	            Ok(r) => r,
   701	            Err(e) => {
   702	                tracing::warn!(error = %e, "failed to parse registry file");
   703	                return Ok(());
   704	            }
   705	        };
   706	
   707	        for entry in &raw_reg.workers {
   708	            // Skip our own entry.
   709	            if entry.id == self.qualified_id {
   710	                continue;
   711	            }
   712	
   713	            // Check if the PID is dead.
   714	            if crate::registry::is_pid_alive(entry.pid) {
   715	                continue;
   716	            }
   717	
   718	            // Dead worker found — deregister it.
   719	            match self.registry.deregister(&entry.id) {
   720	                Ok(()) => {

     1	//! Hierarchical configuration loading and validation.
     2	//!
     3	//! Resolution order (later layers override earlier):
     4	//! 1. Built-in defaults
     5	//! 2. Global config file (`~/.config/needle/config.yaml`)
     6	//! 3. Workspace config file (`.needle.yaml`)
     7	//! 4. Environment variables (`NEEDLE_*`)
     8	//! 5. CLI arguments (highest precedence)
     9	//!
    10	//! Config is loaded once at boot and never reloaded.
    11	//!
    12	//! Leaf module — depends only on `types`.

    29	/// A single routing rule mapping model patterns to adapters.
    30	///
    31	/// Rules are evaluated in order; the first matching rule determines the adapter.
    32	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    33	pub struct RoutingRule {
    34	    /// Regex or glob pattern to match against model names.
    35	    ///
    36	    /// Patterns are matched against the model name only (not provider prefixes).
    37	    /// Examples: `"sonnet"`, `"opus"`, `"claude-sonnet-4-6"`, `"(claude-)?(sonnet|opus).*"`.
    38	    pub match_model: String,
    39	
    40	    /// Adapter to use for matching models (e.g., `claude-print`, `claude-code-glm-4.7`).
    41	    pub adapter: String,
    42	}
    43	
    44	/// Agent routing configuration.
    45	///
    46	/// Maps model name patterns to adapters. When a bead specifies a model,
    47	/// the routing rules are evaluated in order to determine which adapter to use.
    48	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    49	pub struct RoutingConfig {
    50	    /// Ordered list of routing rules (first match wins).
    51	    #[serde(default)]
    52	    pub rules: Vec<RoutingRule>,
    53	
    54	    /// Fallback adapter when no rules match (defaults to `agent.default`).
    55	    #[serde(default)]
    56	    pub default_adapter: Option<String>,
    57	
    58	    /// When true, fail if no routing rule matches instead of falling back.
    59	    ///
    60	    /// If set to true and no rule matches the model:
    61	    /// - The bead dispatch fails immediately
    62	    /// - A `RoutingFailed` telemetry event is emitted
    63	    /// - No fallback to `agent.default` or `default_adapter` occurs
    64	    ///
    65	    /// Default: false (fallback behavior for backward compatibility).
    66	    #[serde(default)]
    67	    pub strict: bool,
    68	}

    70	/// Process timeout limits configuration.
    71	///
    72	/// Defines timeout parameters for agent process execution, separating
    73	/// timeout configuration from other agent settings.
    74	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    75	pub struct ProcessLimits {
    76	    /// Idle timeout duration (None means disabled).
    77	    ///
    78	    /// When set, the agent process will be terminated if no stdout/stderr
    79	    /// activity occurs for this duration. This prevents hung processes from
    80	    /// blocking indefinitely when they stop producing output but don't exit.
    81	    ///
    82	    /// Set to `None` to disable idle timeout detection (processes can run
    83	    /// indefinitely as long as they produce no output).
    84	    ///
    85	    /// # Examples
    86	    ///
    87	    /// ```yaml
    88	    /// # Disable idle timeout (processes can hang indefinitely)
    89	    /// process_limits:
    90	    ///     idle_timeout: null
    91	    ///
    92	    /// # 5 minute idle timeout
    93	    /// process_limits:
    94	    ///     idle_timeout: 300s
    95	    ///
    96	    /// # 30 second idle timeout
    97	    /// process_limits:
    98	    ///     idle_timeout: 30s
    99	    /// ```
   100	    #[serde(default)]
   101	    pub idle_timeout: Option<u64>,
   102	}

   434	/// Backend identifier for the resolved bead CLI.

   438	    Bf,

   452	/// Resolve the bead CLI binary path from configuration.
   453	///
   454	/// Takes a `BeadCliConfig` and returns the backend type and binary path.
   455	/// This replaces all five hardcoded resolution sites across the codebase.
   456	///
   457	/// # Resolution Order
   458	///
   459	/// - If `explicit_path` is set, uses that path directly (backend detection skipped)
   460	/// - `auto` backend: tries bead-rs and bead-forge candidates for diagnostics
   461	/// - `bf` backend: tries bf → ~/.local/bin/bf
   462	/// - `bead` backend: tries bead → ~/.local/bin/bead → /usr/local/cargo/bin/bead
   463	///
   464	/// # Errors
   465	///
   466	/// Returns an error if no matching binary is found. The error message lists
   467	/// all attempted paths.
   468	pub fn resolve_bead_cli(config: &BeadCliConfig) -> Result<(Backend, PathBuf)> {
   469	    // If an explicit path is set, the configured backend remains authoritative.
   470	    // Inferring the dialect from an arbitrary filename would make renamed or
   471	    // wrapper binaries silently select the wrong command grammar.
   472	    if let Some(ref path) = config.path {
   473	        if path.exists() {
   474	            let backend = match config.backend {
   475	                BeadBackend::Bf => Backend::Bf,
   476	                BeadBackend::Br | BeadBackend::Bead => Backend::Bead,
   477	                BeadBackend::Auto => detect_backend_from_path(path)?,
   478	            };
   479	            return Ok((backend, path.clone()));
   480	        } else {
   481	            bail!("explicit bead CLI path does not exist: {}", path.display());
   482	        }
   483	    }
   484	
   485	    let home = std::env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_default();
   486	
   487	    match config.backend {
   488	        BeadBackend::Bf => {
   489	            // bf only: PATH → ~/.local/bin/bf
   490	            let path = find_on_path("bf")
   491	                .or_else(|_| {
   492	                    let candidate = PathBuf::from(format!("{home}/.local/bin/bf"));
   493	                    if is_executable(&candidate) {
   494	                        Ok(candidate)
   495	                    } else {
   496	                        Err(anyhow!("bf not found"))
   497	                    }
   498	                })
   499	                .context("bf CLI not found (checked PATH, ~/.local/bin/bf)")?;
   500	            Ok((Backend::Bf, path))
   501	        }
   502	        BeadBackend::Br | BeadBackend::Bead => {
   503	            // bead only: PATH → ~/.local/bin/bead → /usr/local/cargo/bin/bead
   504	            let path = find_on_path("bead")
   505	                .or_else(|_| {
   506	                    let candidate = PathBuf::from(format!("{home}/.local/bin/bead"));
   507	                    if is_executable(&candidate) {
   508	                        Ok(candidate)
   509	                    } else {
   510	                        Err(anyhow!("bead not found"))
   511	                    }
   512	                })
   513	                .or_else(|_| {
   514	                    let candidate = PathBuf::from("/usr/local/cargo/bin/bead");
   515	                    if is_executable(&candidate) {
   516	                        Ok(candidate)
   517	                    } else {
   518	                        Err(anyhow!("bead not found"))
   519	                    }
   520	                })
   521	                .context(
   522	                    "bead CLI not found (checked PATH, ~/.local/bin/bead, /usr/local/cargo/bin/bead)",
   523	                )?;
   524	            Ok((Backend::Bead, path))
   525	        }
   526	        BeadBackend::Auto => {
   527	            // Auto is diagnostics-only; explicit workspace binding remains
   528	            // mandatory for production store construction.
   529	
   530	            // Per ADR-013: auto detection prefers bead, then bf, then br
   531	            // Try bead first
   532	            if let Ok(path) = find_on_path("bead") {
   533	                return Ok((Backend::Bead, path));
   534	            }
   535	            let bead_local = PathBuf::from(format!("{home}/.local/bin/bead"));
   536	            if is_executable(&bead_local) {
   537	                return Ok((Backend::Bead, bead_local));
   538	            }
   539	            let bead_cargo = PathBuf::from("/usr/local/cargo/bin/bead");
   540	            if is_executable(&bead_cargo) {
   541	                return Ok((Backend::Bead, bead_cargo));
   542	            }
   543	
   544	            // Then bf
   545	            if let Ok(path) = find_on_path("bf") {
   546	                return Ok((Backend::Bf, path));
   547	            }
   548	            let bf_local = PathBuf::from(format!("{home}/.local/bin/bf"));
   549	            if is_executable(&bf_local) {
   550	                return Ok((Backend::Bf, bf_local));
   551	            }
   552	
   553	            // Nothing found
   554	            bail!(
   555	                "no bead CLI found (tried: bead on PATH, {home}/.local/bin/bead, /usr/local/cargo/bin/bead, bf on PATH, {home}/.local/bin/bf)"
   556	            )
   557	        }
   558	    }
   559	}
   560	
   561	/// Resolve an executable against the current `PATH` without process-global
   562	/// caching. Backend selection is workspace-scoped, and tests and embedders may
   563	/// intentionally resolve different environments in one NEEDLE process.
   564	fn find_on_path(binary: &str) -> Result<PathBuf> {
   565	    let path = std::env::var_os("PATH").ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("PATH is not set"))?;
   566	    std::env::split_paths(&path)
   567	        .map(|directory| directory.join(binary))
   568	        .find(|candidate| is_executable(candidate))
   569	        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("{binary} not found on PATH"))
   570	}
   571	
   572	#[cfg(unix)]
   573	fn is_executable(path: &Path) -> bool {
   574	    use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
   575	
   576	    path.metadata()
   577	        .map(|metadata| metadata.is_file() && metadata.permissions().mode() & 0o111 != 0)
   578	        .unwrap_or(false)
   579	}
   580	
   581	#[cfg(not(unix))]
   582	fn is_executable(path: &Path) -> bool {
   583	    path.is_file()
   584	}
   585	
   586	/// Detect the backend type from a binary path.
   587	///
   588	/// Infers the backend from the filename: "bf" selects bead-forge; every other
   589	/// name selects bead-rs.
   590	fn detect_backend_from_path(path: &Path) -> Result<Backend> {
   591	    let file_name = path
   592	        .file_name()
   593	        .and_then(|n| n.to_str())
   594	        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("invalid binary path: no filename"))?;
   595	
   596	    match file_name {
   597	        "bf" => Ok(Backend::Bf),
   598	        _ => Ok(Backend::Bead), // Default to Bead for unknown names
   599	    }
   600	}

     1	//! Abstract bead store interface and CLI implementations.
     2	//!
     3	//! NEEDLE interacts with beads exclusively through the `BeadStore` trait. The
     4	//! default implementation shells out to `bf` (bead-forge) with `--json` output.
     5	//! JSON parsing failures are explicit errors — never silently treated as empty
     6	//! results (v1 bug).
     7	//!
     8	//! The trait is `Send + Sync` because it is called from async worker tasks.
     9	//!
    10	//! `CliBeadStore` binds one backend descriptor to one executable, preventing
    11	//! command grammar and binary identity from being mixed accidentally.
    12	//!
    13	//! IMPORTANT: authors of the `bead-rs`/beads_rust descriptor must probe the
    14	//! actual beads_rust binary (including its help and output), not infer its
    15	//! dialect from this module, `CliBeadStore`, or the bead-forge descriptor.
    16	//!
    17	//! Depends on: `types`.
    18	
    19	mod backend;
    20	mod cli_store;
    21	mod strategies;
    22	
    23	use std::collections::HashSet;
    24	use std::path::Path;
    25	use std::path::PathBuf;
    26	use std::sync::Arc;
    27	
    28	use anyhow::{bail, Context, Result};
    29	use async_trait::async_trait;
    30	
    31	use crate::types::{Bead, BeadId, ClaimResult};
    32	use tracing::{debug, warn};
    33	
    34	// Re-export the implementations so consumers don't need to change their imports
    35	pub use backend::{
    36	    builtin_bead_backends, load_bead_backends, BeadBackend, BeadBackendCapabilities,
    37	    BeadBackendErrorMarkers, BeadBackendQuirk, BeadOperationSpec, ParseShape,

    41	/// Open the bead store explicitly bound by the target workspace's resolved
    42	/// configuration. This is the production entry point: executable discovery
    43	/// alone is never treated as evidence of store ownership.
    44	pub fn open_configured(
    45	    config: &crate::config::BeadCliConfig,
    46	    workspace: PathBuf,
    47	    model: Option<String>,
    48	    harness: Option<String>,
    49	    harness_version: Option<String>,
    50	) -> Result<Arc<dyn BeadStore>> {
    51	    if matches!(config.backend, crate::config::BeadBackend::Auto) {
    52	        bail!(
    53	            "workspace {} has no authoritative bead backend binding; set bead_cli.backend in {}",
    54	            workspace.display(),
    55	            workspace.join(".needle.yaml").display()
    56	        );
    57	    }
    58	
    59	    let (backend, binary) = crate::config::resolve_bead_cli(config).with_context(|| {
    60	        format!(
    61	            "failed to resolve bead_cli.backend for workspace {}",
    62	            workspace.display()
    63	        )
    64	    })?;
    65	    verify_backend_identity(&backend, &binary, &workspace)?;
    66	    if backend == crate::config::Backend::Bead {
    67	        verify_bead_rs_capabilities(&binary, &workspace)?;
    68	    }
    69	
    70	    match backend {
    71	        crate::config::Backend::Bf => {
    72	            let descriptor = builtin_bead_backends()
    73	                .into_iter()
    74	                .find(|candidate| candidate.name == "bead-forge")
    75	                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("built-in bead-forge descriptor is missing"))?;
    76	            Ok(Arc::new(CliBeadStore::new(
    77	                descriptor,
    78	                binary,
    79	                workspace,
    80	                model,
    81	                harness,
    82	                harness_version,
    83	            )?))
    84	        }
    85	        crate::config::Backend::Bead => {
    86	            let descriptor = builtin_bead_backends()
    87	                .into_iter()
    88	                .find(|candidate| candidate.name == "bead-rs")
    89	                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("built-in bead-rs descriptor is missing"))?;
    90	            Ok(Arc::new(CliBeadStore::new(
    91	                descriptor,
    92	                binary,
    93	                workspace,
    94	                model,
    95	                harness,
    96	                harness_version,
    97	            )?))
    98	        }
    99	    }
   100	}
   101	
   102	fn verify_backend_identity(
   103	    backend: &crate::config::Backend,
   104	    binary: &Path,
   105	    workspace: &Path,
   106	) -> Result<()> {
   107	    use regex::Regex;
   108	    use std::io::Read;
   109	    use std::process::Stdio;
   110	
   111	    // Get the backend descriptor for this backend type
   112	    let descriptor_name = match backend {
   113	        crate::config::Backend::Bf => "bead-forge",
   114	        crate::config::Backend::Bead => "bead-rs",
   115	    };
   116	
   117	    let descriptor = builtin_bead_backends()
   118	        .into_iter()
   119	        .find(|d| d.name == descriptor_name)
   120	        .ok_or_else(|| {
   121	            anyhow::anyhow!(
   122	                "built-in backend descriptor '{}' not found",
   123	                descriptor_name
   124	            )
   125	        })?;
   126	
   127	    let mut child = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_child(
   128	        || {
   129	            std::process::Command::new(binary)
   130	                .args(&descriptor.version_command)
   131	                .stdout(Stdio::piped())
   132	                .stderr(Stdio::piped())
   133	                .spawn()
   134	        },
   135	        5,  // max_attempts
   136	        20, // backoff_ms
   137	    )
   138	    .with_context(|| {
   139	        format!(
   140	            "failed to inspect bead CLI identity at {}",
   141	            binary.display()
   142	        )
   143	    })?;
   144	    let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_secs(5);
   145	    let status = loop {
   146	        if let Some(status) = child.try_wait().with_context(|| {
   147	            format!(
   148	                "failed waiting for bead CLI identity at {}",
   149	                binary.display()
   150	            )
   151	        })? {
   152	            break status;
   153	        }
   154	        if std::time::Instant::now() >= deadline {
   155	            let _ = child.kill();
   156	            let _ = child.wait();
   157	            bail!(
   158	                "timed out verifying bead backend identity for workspace {} at {}",
   159	                workspace.display(),
   160	                binary.display()
   161	            );
   162	        }
   163	        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(10));
   164	    };
   165	    let mut stdout = Vec::new();
   166	    let mut stderr = Vec::new();
   167	    if let Some(mut stream) = child.stdout.take() {
   168	        stream.read_to_end(&mut stdout)?;
   169	    }
   170	    if let Some(mut stream) = child.stderr.take() {
   171	        stream.read_to_end(&mut stderr)?;
   172	    }
   173	    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&stdout);
   174	    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&stderr);
   175	    let identity = format!("{stdout}{stderr}");
   176	
   177	    if !status.success() {
   178	        bail!(
   179	            "bead backend identity check failed for workspace {}: {} --version exited with code {} (output: {:?})",
   180	            workspace.display(),
   181	            binary.display(),
   182	            status.code().unwrap_or(-1),
   183	            identity.trim()
   184	        );
   185	    }
   186	
   187	    // Parse the version output using the descriptor's identity_pattern
   188	    let identity_pattern = Regex::new(&descriptor.identity_pattern).with_context(|| {
   189	        format!(
   190	            "invalid identity_pattern regex for backend '{}': {:?}",
   191	            descriptor.name, descriptor.identity_pattern
   192	        )
   193	    })?;
   194	
   195	    let trimmed_output = identity.trim_start();
   196	    if !identity_pattern.is_match(trimmed_output) {
   197	        bail!(
   198	            "bead backend identity mismatch for workspace {}: binary at {} reported version {:?}, which does not match expected pattern {:?} for backend '{}'",
   199	            workspace.display(),
   200	            binary.display(),
   201	            trimmed_output,
   202	            descriptor.identity_pattern,
   203	            descriptor.name
   204	        );
   205	    }
   206	
   207	    // Extract the backend name from the version output
   208	    // The pattern captures the name at the start (e.g., "bf " or "bead ")
   209	    let captured_name = trimmed_output
   210	        .split_whitespace()
   211	        .next()
   212	        .ok_or_else(|| {
   213	            anyhow::anyhow!(
   214	                "bead backend identity extraction failed for workspace {}: binary at {} reported empty version output",
   215	                workspace.display(),
   216	                binary.display()
   217	            )
   218	        })?;
   219	
   220	    // Map the captured name to the expected backend name
   221	    // Both "bf" and "bead" should map to their respective backend names
   222	    let expected_names = match descriptor.name.as_str() {
   223	        "bead-forge" => vec!["bf", "bead-forge"],
   224	        "bead-rs" => vec!["bead", "bead-rs"],
   225	        _ => vec![descriptor.name.as_str()],
   226	    };
   227	
   228	    if !expected_names.contains(&captured_name) {
   229	        bail!(
   230	            "bead backend identity mismatch for workspace {}: binary at {} reported name {:?}, but expected one of {:?} for backend '{}'",
   231	            workspace.display(),
   232	            binary.display(),
   233	            captured_name,
   234	            expected_names,
   235	            descriptor.name
   236	        );
   237	    }
   238	
   239	    Ok(())
   240	}

   242	fn verify_bead_rs_capabilities(binary: &Path, workspace: &Path) -> Result<()> {
   243	    let output = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync(
   244	        || {
   245	            std::process::Command::new(binary)
   246	                .args(["capabilities", "--profile", "native-v1"])
   247	                .current_dir(workspace)
   248	                .output()
   249	        },
   250	        5,
   251	        20,
   252	    )
   253	    .with_context(|| {
   254	        format!(
   255	            "failed to probe bead-rs capabilities at {}",
   256	            binary.display()
   257	        )
   258	    })?;
   259	    if !output.status.success() {
   260	        bail!(
   261	            "bead-rs capability probe failed for workspace {} at {}: {}",
   262	            workspace.display(),
   263	            binary.display(),
   264	            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).trim()
   265	        );
   266	    }
   267	    let capabilities: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&output.stdout)
   268	        .with_context(|| format!("invalid bead-rs capability JSON from {}", binary.display()))?;
   269	    if capabilities
   270	        .get("implementation")
   271	        .and_then(|value| value.as_str())
   272	        != Some("bead-rs")
   273	        || capabilities
   274	            .get("atomic_claim")
   275	            .and_then(|value| value.as_bool())
   276	            != Some(true)
   277	    {
   278	        bail!(
   279	            "bead-rs capability mismatch for workspace {}: expected implementation=bead-rs and atomic_claim=true",
   280	            workspace.display()
